summary: The design fits the existing ingestion boundaries but has several persistence and identity hazards. The highest risks are source-slice deletion of document links, swallowed store failures, non-atomic non-SQLite backends, and Fireflies/ADR rerun identity handling.

suggestions.title: Keep the document page outside the orchestrator source slice
suggestions.rationale: `WikiIngestOrchestrator` replaces all pages for a source, while `replace_source_slice` deletes every page and edge touching the old ids unless the ids are included in the replacement set. If the new `doc:<slug>` page uses the orchestrator source_id but is not passed into that replacement, reruns delete the document page and incoming links from other documents. Use a separate stable source identity, or make the inbox-owned composite slice explicitly include and preserve the document page and its inbound edges.

suggestions.title: Do not archive after the current orchestrator reports a false success
suggestions.rationale: The orchestrator catches WikiStore synchronization failures and continues, and it also treats manifest and bookkeeping failures as warnings before returning `status="ok"`. An inbox wrapper that trusts `IngestReport.status` can archive a file whose retrieval page or provenance was never persisted. Add an inbox-specific strict persistence result and verify the document page, child pages, projection, and source metadata before moving the original.

suggestions.title: Define crash consistency per backend instead of assuming replace_source_slice is atomic
suggestions.rationale: The abstract store documents atomic replacement, but the memory backend deletes old pages one at a time, writes replacement pages, then rewrites the index; the Arango backend similarly performs delete and upsert operations as separate calls. A process crash can leave a partial slice even though the inbox contract promises resumability. Either add a real transaction/staging capability, introduce a recovery journal, or explicitly restrict crash-safe inbox processing to backends that can provide the guarantee.

suggestions.title: Extend the projection contract for free-form tags and the tag category
suggestions.rationale: `WikiPageRecord` has no tag collection and `page_frontmatter()` always emits only the page category as `tags`; the memory renderer delegates to that function. Therefore the required normalized document tags cannot be rendered through the stated existing contract without ad hoc body manipulation. Define a render-only tags input or a persisted page metadata field, add the `tag` category contract where enum-based callers need it, and test SQLite, memory, and export output for identical frontmatter.

suggestions.title: Make Fireflies re-ingestion preserve the existing source identity
suggestions.rationale: `find_by_external_id()` returns an existing manifest entry, but the orchestrator then resolves by URI and calls `add_source()`; a new inbox path therefore creates a new path-derived source unless the processor explicitly repoints the existing entry first. `update_source_uri()` exists but requires the new file to exist and rejects URI ownership conflicts. Specify and test the sequence that transfers the existing source to the inbox path, re-ingests it, and transfers it to the new archive path without creating a second source or losing external_id.

suggestions.title: Make ADR candidate creation idempotent and review-safe
suggestions.rationale: `DecisionRepository.save(record, None)` is insert-only and returns a revision conflict when the page already exists. The ADR models also require complete evidence fields, including repository-relative path, line range, and source hash. A rerun that emits the same candidate must use a deterministic candidate id and treat an existing equivalent/reviewed record as reused, rather than overwriting or failing the inbox run.

suggestions.title: Add force semantics below the CLI layer
suggestions.rationale: The existing triage router unconditionally performs Stage-0 duplicate checks by URI and content hash; it has no force parameter. Implementing `--force` only in the command would either fail to bypass the duplicate rejection or bypass the whole triage policy. Pass an explicit force policy into the router, bypass duplicate checks only, and retain size, suffix, sensitive-content, and taxonomy validation.

suggestions.title: Fail closed on malformed structured classification and link responses
suggestions.rationale: `PageIndexLLMAdapter.ask_structured()` can return a Pydantic instance, a validated dict, a list, or an empty parsed value depending on provider behavior. The inbox must reject anything that is not the expected model, and must separately validate kind membership, tag limits, candidate-id membership, relation vocabulary, duplicate selections, and self-links. Falling back to `default_kind` should apply only to an explicitly unknown kind, not to malformed or missing model output.

suggestions.title: Serialize inbox claims and persistence against concurrent writers
suggestions.rationale: The project already has `wiki_write_lock`, and build/upsert use it to prevent concurrent store mutations. Two inbox processes otherwise can both triage the same file, create competing pages, race on archive naming, and stage conflicting git removals. Reuse the lock for the persistence/archive critical section and define whether LLM work occurs under it or use a per-file claim/state marker so duplicate processing cannot occur.

suggestions.title: Constrain configurable inbox and archive paths
suggestions.rationale: `WikiProjectConfig.storage_path()` resolves a relative path by joining it to the repository root, while `resolve_sources()` accepts arbitrary existing paths and follows normal filesystem resolution. New configurable inbox/archive paths need validation against repository/storage boundaries, rejection of the archive inside the inbox, and explicit symlink behavior; otherwise a typo or symlink can move unrelated files and stage their deletion.
